questions.stem: What does the man ask the woman to do?

options.A: Stop worrying about him.
options.B: Keep away from the statue.
options.C: Take a picture of him.
options.D: Put on a smile for the photo.

questions.cn: 男士请女士做什么？

optionsCn.A: 别再为他担心。
optionsCn.C: 给他拍张照片。
optionsCn.D: 拍照时笑一笑。

questions.stem: What does the man dream of?

options.A: Gaining great fame on the Internet.
options.B: Publishing a collection of his photos.
options.C: Collecting the best photos in the world.
options.D: Becoming a professional photographer.

questions.cn: 男士的梦想是什么？

optionsCn.A: 在网上获得大名气。
optionsCn.B: 出版自己的摄影作品集。
optionsCn.C: 收集世界上最好的照片。
optionsCn.D: 成为职业摄影师。

questions.stem: What has the man been busy doing recently?

options.A: Surfing various websites and collecting photos.
options.B: Editing his pictures and posting them online.
options.C: Following similar accounts to compare notes.
options.D: Studying the pictures in popular social media.

optionsCn.A: 浏览各种网站并收集照片。
optionsCn.C: 关注类似账号来交流心得。
optionsCn.D: 研究热门社交媒体上的图片。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her photos?

options.A: They are far from satisfactory.
options.B: They are mostly taken by her mom.
options.C: They make an impressive album.
options.D: They record her fond memories.

questions.cn: 关于自己的照片，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们远不能令人满意。
optionsCn.C: 它们做成了一本很棒的照片集。
optionsCn.D: 它们记录了她美好的回忆。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: Do you mind taking my photo with the statue over there?
lines.cn: M：你能帮我拍张我和那边那座雕像的合影吗？

lines.t: M: I think it will make a great shot.
lines.cn: M：我觉得拍出来会很好看。

lines.t: F: Sure, no worries.
lines.cn: F：当然，没问题。

lines.t: F: You're always taking photos.
lines.cn: F：你总是拍照片。

lines.t: F: What do you do with all the photos you take?
lines.cn: F：你拍的这么多照片都拿来做什么？

lines.t: M: Well, don't laugh.
lines.cn: M：嗯，别笑我。

lines.t: M: My dream is to become an online celebrity of sorts.
lines.cn: M：我的梦想是成为某种意义上的网络红人。

lines.t: F: You're not serious, are you?
lines.cn: F：你不是认真的吧？

lines.t: M: I am completely.
lines.cn: M：我完全是认真的。

lines.t: M: I just got the idea a few months ago after posting some holiday photos on my social media accounts.
lines.cn: M：几个月前我在社交媒体账号上发了一些假期照片之后，才有了这个想法。

lines.t: M: A lot of people liked my photos and started asking me for travel tips.
lines.cn: M：很多人喜欢我的照片，开始向我要旅行建议。

lines.t: M: So I figured I'd give it a go.
lines.cn: M：所以我想，那就试试看吧。

lines.t: M: I post a lot on social media anyway, so I've got nothing to lose.
lines.cn: M：反正我在社交媒体上本来就发得很多，也没什么可损失的。

lines.t: F: I guess that's true.
lines.cn: F：这倒是真的。

lines.t: F: So what do you have to do to become internet famous?
lines.cn: F：那要成为网络名人得做些什么呢？

lines.t: M: Surprisingly, a lot more than I did as a hobby.
lines.cn: M：出乎意料，比我当作爱好时做的多得多。

lines.t: M: Recently, I've been spending a lot more time editing photos, posting online, and clearing storage on my phone.
lines.cn: M：最近我花了更多时间修图、发帖，还有清理手机存储空间。

lines.t: M: It's always full now.
lines.cn: M：现在手机总是满的。

lines.t: F: That doesn't sound like too much work.
lines.cn: F：听起来工作量也不算太大。

lines.t: M: Well, there's more to it.
lines.cn: M：嗯，还有更多。

lines.t: M: I spent all last weekend researching what topics are popular, what words to use in captions, and similar accounts to follow.
lines.cn: M：上周末我整整花了两天研究哪些话题受欢迎、配文该用什么词、该关注哪些类似的账号。

lines.t: M: It really was a lot to take in.
lines.cn: M：要吸收的东西真的太多了。

lines.t: M: And I was up well past midnight.
lines.cn: M：而且我熬到过了半夜才睡。

lines.t: M: I'd say it's paying off though.
lines.cn: M：不过我觉得这是有回报的。

lines.t: M: I increased the number of people following my accounts by 15% already.
lines.cn: M：我的账号关注人数已经增加了 15%。

lines.t: F: That is impressive.
lines.cn: F：那很了不起。

lines.t: F: I guess I never thought much about all the effort behind the scene.
lines.cn: F：我想我从没多想这背后要付出这么多努力。

lines.t: F: Now that I think about it, there's always something wrong with my photos as it is.
lines.cn: F：说起来，我的照片现在本来就总有点问题。

lines.t: F: Half smiles, closed eyes, messy hair.
lines.cn: F：笑到一半、闭着眼、头发乱。

lines.t: F: I hope you have better luck than I do.
lines.cn: F：希望你运气比我好。

lines.t: F: Then again, I think the only person interested in my photos is my mum.
lines.cn: F：不过话说回来，我猜唯一对我照片感兴趣的人就是我妈。

questions.stem: What does the man say is physics today?

options.A: A journal reporting the latest progress in physics.
options.B: An introductory course of modern physics.
options.C: An occasion for physicists to exchange ideas.
options.D: A series of interviews with outstanding physicists.

questions.cn: 男士说《今日物理》是什么？

optionsCn.A: 一份报道物理学最新进展的期刊。
optionsCn.B: 一门现代物理学的入门课程。
optionsCn.C: 一个物理学家交流想法的场合。
optionsCn.D: 一系列对杰出物理学家的访谈。

options.A: The future of the physical world.
options.B: The origin of the universe.
options.C: Sources of radiation.
options.D: Particle theory.

questions.cn: 这位女物理学家的主要研究领域是什么？

optionsCn.A: 物理世界的未来。
optionsCn.C: 辐射的来源。
optionsCn.D: 粒子理论。

questions.stem: What is the woman interested in?

options.A: How matter collides with anti-matter.
options.B: Whether the universe will turn barren.
options.C: Why there exists anti-matter.
options.D: Why there is a universe at all.

questions.cn: 女士感兴趣的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 物质如何与反物质碰撞。
optionsCn.C: 为什么存在反物质。
optionsCn.D: 宇宙究竟为何存在。

questions.stem: What seems to be the finding of the recent study?

options.A: Matter and anti-matter are opposites of each other.
options.B: Anti-matter allowed humans to come into existence.
options.C: The universe formed due to a sufficient amount of matter.
options.D: Anti-matter exists in very high-temperature environments.

questions.cn: 最近这项研究的发现似乎是什么？

optionsCn.A: 物质和反物质彼此对立。
optionsCn.B: 反物质使人类得以存在。
optionsCn.C: 宇宙因物质数量充足而形成。
optionsCn.D: 反物质存在于极高温度的环境中。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: Good evening and welcome to Physics Today.
lines.cn: M：晚上好，欢迎收看《今日物理》。

lines.t: M: Here we interview some of the greatest minds in physics as they help us to understand some of the most complicated theories.
lines.cn: M：在这里，我们采访物理学界一些最杰出的头脑，请他们帮我们理解一些最复杂的理论。

lines.t: M: Today, I'm very pleased to welcome Dr.
lines.cn: M：今天我非常高兴地欢迎

lines.t: M: Melissa Phillips, Professor of Theoretical Physics.
lines.cn: M：梅丽莎·菲利普斯博士，理论物理学教授。

lines.t: M: She's here to tell us a little about what it is she studies.
lines.cn: M：她来这里给我们讲讲她的研究内容。

lines.t: M: Dr.
lines.cn: M：博士，

lines.t: M: Phillips, you seem to study everything.
lines.cn: M：菲利普斯，您似乎什么都研究。

lines.t: F: I guess that would be fair to say.
lines.cn: F：我想这么说也算公道。

lines.t: F: I spend most of my time studying the Big Bang theory and where our universe came from.
lines.cn: F：我大部分时间都在研究大爆炸理论，以及我们的宇宙从何而来。

lines.t: M: Can you tell us a little about that?
lines.cn: M：能给我们简单讲讲吗？

lines.t: F: Well, I'm very interested in why the universe exists at all.
lines.cn: F：嗯，我非常感兴趣的是：宇宙究竟为何存在。

lines.t: F: That may sound odd, but the fact is, at the moment of the Big Bang, both matter and antimatter were created.
lines.cn: F：这听起来也许奇怪，但事实是，在大爆炸那一刻，物质和反物质都被创造了出来。

lines.t: F: For a short time, and I mean just a fraction of a second, the whole universe was a super hot soup of radiation filled with these particles.
lines.cn: F：在很短的时间里——我指的只是几分之一秒——整个宇宙是一锅充满这些粒子的超高温辐射浓汤。

lines.t: F: So, what's baffled scientists for so long is, why is there a universe at all?
lines.cn: F：所以，长期困扰科学家的问题是：宇宙究竟为何存在？

lines.t: F: That's because matter and antimatter are basically opposites of each other.
lines.cn: F：这是因为物质和反物质基本上是彼此的对立面。

lines.t: F: They are exactly alike, except that they have opposite electrical charges.
lines.cn: F：它们完全相同，只是电荷相反。

lines.t: M: So, when they collide, they destroy each other?
lines.cn: M：那么，它们相撞时就会彼此湮灭？

lines.t: F: Exactly.
lines.cn: F：正是。

lines.t: F: So, during the first few moments of the Big Bang, the universe was extremely hot and very small.
lines.cn: F：所以，在大爆炸最初的那几个瞬间，宇宙极其炽热而且非常小。

lines.t: F: Matter, and the now more exotic antimatter, would have had little space to avoid each other.
lines.cn: F：物质以及更为奇异的反物质，几乎没有空间可以彼此避开。

lines.t: F: This means that they should have totally wiped each other out, leaving the universe completely barren.
lines.cn: F：这意味着它们本应完全相互抵消，让宇宙变得一片荒芜。

lines.t: M: But a recent study seems to point to the fact that when matter and antimatter were first created, there were slightly more particles of matter, which allowed the universe we all live in to form?
lines.cn: M：但最近一项研究似乎指出，物质和反物质最初被创造出来时，物质的粒子略多一些，这才使我们所生活的宇宙得以形成？

lines.t: F: Exactly.
lines.cn: F：正是。

lines.t: F: Because there was slightly more matter, the collisions quickly depleted all the antimatter and left just enough matter to create stars, planets, and eventually us.
lines.cn: F：因为物质稍多一些，碰撞很快耗尽所有反物质，只剩下刚好足够的物质来形成恒星、行星，最终还有我们。

options.D: She woke up finding herself in another country.

optionsCn.B: 她醒来时说话带上了不同的口音。

options.B: It has not yet found any effective treatment.
options.C: It leaves the patient with a distorted memory.

optionsCn.A: 它通常由中风或脑损伤引起。
optionsCn.B: 它尚未找到任何有效的治疗方法。

options.A: British.
options.B: Irish.
options.C: Russian.
options.D: Australian.

optionsCn.A: 英国口音。
optionsCn.C: 俄罗斯口音。
optionsCn.D: 澳大利亚口音。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: In this week's edition of special series on bizarre medical conditions, there's a report of the case of Michelle Myers.
lines.cn: 在本周那期关于奇特医学病症的专题系列中，有一篇关于米歇尔·迈尔斯病例的报道。

lines.t: Myers is an American woman who woke up one day speaking with a British accent, even though she's lived in the United States all her life.
lines.cn: 迈尔斯是一位美国女性，有一天醒来时说起了一口英国口音，尽管她一辈子都生活在美国。

lines.t: In 2015, Myers went to bed with a terrible headache.
lines.cn: 2015 年，迈尔斯带着剧烈的头痛上床睡觉。

lines.t: She woke up sounding like someone from England.
lines.cn: 醒来后她说话听起来像英格兰人。

lines.t: Her British accent has remained for the past two years.
lines.cn: 她的英国口音在过去两年里一直保持着。

lines.t: Previously, Myers had woken up speaking in Irish and Australian accents.
lines.cn: 此前，迈尔斯还曾在醒来时带着爱尔兰口音和澳大利亚口音。

lines.t: However, on both of those occasions, the accents lasted for only a week.
lines.cn: 不过那两次，口音都只持续了一周。

lines.t: Myers has been diagnosed with Foreign Accent Syndrome.
lines.cn: 迈尔斯被诊断患有外国口音综合征。

lines.t: It's a disorder in which a person experiences a sudden change to their speech so that they sound like they are speaking in a foreign accent.
lines.cn: 这是一种障碍，患者的言语会突然改变，听起来像是在用外国口音说话。

lines.t: The condition is most often caused by a stroke or traumatic brain injury.
lines.cn: 这种病症最常由中风或创伤性脑损伤引起。

lines.t: Although people with the syndrome have intelligible speech, their manner of speaking is altered in terms of timing and tongue placement, which may distort their pronunciation.
lines.cn: 尽管患者的言语可以听懂，但他们说话在节律和舌头位置方面发生了变化，这可能会使发音扭曲。

lines.t: The result is that they may sound foreign when speaking their native language.
lines.cn: 结果是，他们讲母语时听起来却像外国人。

lines.t: It's not clear whether Myers has experienced a stroke or other brain damage, but she also has a separate medical condition which can result in loose joints, easily bruised skin, and other problems.
lines.cn: 目前尚不清楚迈尔斯是否经历过中风或其他脑损伤，但她还患有另一种疾病，会导致关节松弛、皮肤容易淤青等问题。

lines.t: Foreign Accent Syndrome is rare, with only about 60 cases reported within the past century.
lines.cn: 外国口音综合征很罕见，过去一个世纪里仅报告了约 60 例。

lines.t: However, a different American woman reportedly spoke with a Russian accent in 2010 after she fell down the stairs and hit her head.
lines.cn: 不过据报道，另一位美国女性在 2010 年从楼梯上摔下撞到头之后，说话带上了俄罗斯口音。

questions.stem: What has become so popular recently?

options.A: Water sports.
options.B: Racing in rivers.
options.C: Stories about women swimmers.
options.D: Books about swimming.

questions.cn: 最近什么东西变得如此流行？

optionsCn.A: 水上运动。
optionsCn.C: 关于女性游泳者的故事。
optionsCn.D: 关于游泳的书。

questions.stem: What did Jenny Landreth do recently?

options.A: She succeeded in swimming across the English Channel.
options.B: She published a guide to London's best swimming spots.
options.C: She told her story of adventures to some young swimmers.
options.D: She wrote a book about the history of swimwear in the UK.

questions.cn: 珍妮·兰德雷思最近做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 她成功横渡了英吉利海峡。
optionsCn.B: 她出版了一本伦敦最佳游泳地点指南。
optionsCn.C: 她向一些年轻游泳者讲述了自己的冒险故事。
optionsCn.D: 她写了一本关于英国泳装历史的书。

questions.stem: What do we learn about women in the Victorian era?

options.A: They loved vacationing on the seashore.
options.B: They had a unique notion of modesty.
options.C: They were prohibited from swimming.
options.D: They were fully dressed when swimming.

questions.cn: 关于维多利亚时代的女性，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 她们喜欢在海边度假。
optionsCn.B: 她们有独特的体面观念。
optionsCn.C: 她们被禁止游泳。
optionsCn.D: 她们游泳时穿着完整的衣服。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Gertrude Adelaide?

options.A: She designed lots of appropriate swimwear for women.
options.B: She once successfully competed against men in swimming.
options.C: She was the first woman to swim across the English Channel.
options.D: She was an advocate of women's right to swim in public pools.

questions.cn: 关于格特鲁德·阿德莱德，短文说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 她为女性设计了许多合适的泳装。
optionsCn.B: 她曾在游泳比赛中成功战胜男性。
optionsCn.C: 她是第一位横渡英吉利海峡的女性。
optionsCn.D: 她是女性在公共泳池游泳权利的倡导者。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: There is something about water that makes it a good metaphor for life.
lines.cn: 水身上有某种特质，使它成为人生绝佳的隐喻。

lines.t: That may be one reason why so many people find relief in swimming when life's seas get rough, and it goes some way towards explaining why books about swimming, in which people tackle icy lakes, race in rivers, and overcome oceans, while reflecting on their lives, have recently become so popular.
lines.cn: 这或许正是许多人在人生风浪汹涌时通过游泳获得解脱的原因之一，也在一定程度上解释了：为何那些描写人们挑战冰冷湖水、在河流中竞速、征服大海，同时反思自身人生的游泳书籍近来如此流行。

lines.t: These books reflect a trend particularly strong in Britain, where swimming in pools is declining, but more and more folks are opting for open water.
lines.cn: 这些书反映了一种在英国尤为明显的趋势：在泳池游泳的人越来越少，而越来越多的人选择去开放水域。

lines.t: Wild swimming seems to be especially popular among women.
lines.cn: 野外游泳似乎尤其受女性欢迎。

lines.t: Jenny Landreth recently published a guide to the best swimming spots in London.
lines.cn: 珍妮·兰德雷思最近出版了一本伦敦最佳游泳地点指南。

lines.t: Her new book, Swell, interweaves her own story with a history of female pioneers who accomplished remarkable feats, and paved the way for future generations.
lines.cn: 她的新书《浪涌》把自己的故事与那些女先驱的历史交织在一起——她们成就了非凡壮举，也为后代铺平了道路。

lines.t: Notions of modesty restricted women in the Victorian era, but they still swam.
lines.cn: 维多利亚时代，体面观念束缚着女性，但她们仍然游泳。

lines.t: A bathing machine was rolled down to the seashore, so women would not be seen in swimwear.
lines.cn: 一种更衣车会被推到海边，这样女性就不会被别人看到穿着泳装的样子。

lines.t: In 1892, the Gentlewoman's Book of Sport, described a woman swimming in a heavy dress, boots, hat, gloves, and carrying an umbrella.
lines.cn: 1892 年出版的《淑女运动之书》描述了一位女性穿着厚重的裙子、靴子，戴着帽子和手套，还撑着一把伞在游泳。

lines.t: Eventually, swimming became freer.
lines.cn: 最终，游泳变得更加自由。

lines.t: Mixed bathing was permitted on British beaches in 1901.
lines.cn: 1901 年，英国海滩允许男女同浴。

lines.t: Women won the right to swim in public pools, learned to swim properly, created appropriate swimwear, and, in time, even competed against men.
lines.cn: 女性赢得了在公共泳池游泳的权利，学会了正确的游泳方法，设计出合适的泳装，并最终甚至能与男性同场竞技。

lines.t: The first woman to cross the English Channel was Gertrude Adelaide in 1926.
lines.cn: 1926 年，格特鲁德·阿德莱德成为第一位横渡英吉利海峡的女性。

lines.t: She beat the record by almost two hours, and her father rewarded her with a red sports car.
lines.cn: 她以近两小时的优势打破纪录，父亲奖励了她一辆红色跑车。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What have researchers and law enforcement agencies tried to do?

options.A: Build a machine that can detect lies.
options.B: Develop a magnetic brain scanner.
options.C: Test the credibility of court evidence.
options.D: Win people's complete trust in them.

questions.cn: 研究人员和执法机构一直试图做什么？

optionsCn.A: 制造一台能识破谎言的机器。
optionsCn.C: 检验法庭证据的可信度。
optionsCn.D: 赢得人们对其完全的信任。

questions.stem: How do many brain scientists respond to the Massachusetts company's so-called technological breakthrough?

options.A: They are optimistic about its potential.
options.B: They are sceptical of its reliability.
options.C: They think it is just business promotion.
options.D: They celebrate it with great enthusiasm.

questions.cn: 许多脑科学家如何看待马萨诸塞州那家公司所谓的技术突破？

optionsCn.A: 他们对其潜力感到乐观。
optionsCn.C: 他们认为这不过是商业宣传。
optionsCn.D: 他们热情地为之欢呼。

questions.stem: What does the speaker think of using a high-tech test to determine whether a person is telling the truth?

options.A: It is not to be trusted at all.
options.B: It does not sound economical.
options.C: It may intrude into people's privacy.
options.D: It may lead to overuse in court trials.

questions.cn: 讲话者如何看待用高科技检测来判断一个人是否说真话？

optionsCn.A: 它完全不可信。
optionsCn.C: 它可能侵犯人们的隐私。
optionsCn.D: 它可能在法庭审判中被过度使用。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Today, I'm going to talk about a very special kind of person.
lines.cn: 今天我要讲一种非常特别的人。

lines.t: Psychologists call them Masters of Deception.
lines.cn: 心理学家称他们为“欺骗大师”。

lines.t: Those rare individuals with a natural ability to tell with complete confidence when someone is telling a lie.
lines.cn: 这些罕见的人天生就能十分笃定地判断出别人何时在说谎。

lines.t: For decades, researchers and law enforcement agencies have tried to build a machine that will do the same thing.
lines.cn: 几十年来，研究人员和执法机构一直试图造出一台能做同样事情的机器。

lines.t: Now, a company in Massachusetts says that by using magnetic brain scans, they can determine with 97% accuracy whether someone is telling the truth.
lines.cn: 如今，马萨诸塞州一家公司声称，通过磁场脑部扫描，他们能以 97% 的准确率判断一个人是否在说真话。

lines.t: They hope that the technology will be cleared for use in American courts by early next year.
lines.cn: 他们希望这项技术能在明年初获准用于美国法庭。

lines.t: But is this really the ultimate tool for you, the lawyers of tomorrow?
lines.cn: 但对你们这些未来的律师来说，这真的是终极工具吗？

lines.t: You will not find many brain scientists celebrating this breakthrough.
lines.cn: 你找不到多少脑科学家为这一突破欢呼。

lines.t: The company might be very optimistic, but the ability of their machine to detect deception has not provided credible proof.
lines.cn: 这家公司也许非常乐观，但他们机器识别欺骗的能力并没有提供可信的证据。

lines.t: That's because the technology has not been properly tested in real-world situations.
lines.cn: 这是因为该技术尚未在真实情境中得到充分检验。

lines.t: In life, there are different kinds of lies and diverse contexts in which they're told.
lines.cn: 生活中有各种各样的谎言，说谎的情境也各不相同。

lines.t: These differences may elicit different brain responses.
lines.cn: 这些差异可能引发不同的大脑反应。

lines.t: Does their hypothesis behind the apply in every case?
lines.cn: 他们背后的假设在每一种情况下都成立吗？

lines.t: We don't know the answer because studies done on how reliable this machine is have not yet been duplicated.
lines.cn: 我们不知道答案，因为关于这台机器可靠性的研究尚未被重复验证。

lines.t: Much more research is badly needed.
lines.cn: 急需更多研究。

lines.t: Whether the technology is eventually deemed reliable enough for the courts will ultimately be decided by the judges.
lines.cn: 这项技术最终是否被认为足够可靠、可用于法庭，最终将由法官决定。

lines.t: Let's hope they're wise enough not to be fooled by a machine that claims to determine truthfulness at the flip of a switch.
lines.cn: 但愿他们足够明智，不会被一台声称一按开关就能判定真伪的机器所蒙蔽。

lines.t: They should also be skeptical of the growing tendency to try to reduce all human traits and actions to the level of brain activity.
lines.cn: 他们也应该警惕一种日益增长的趋势：试图把人类所有的特性和行为都简化为大脑活动。

lines.t: Often, they do not map that easily.
lines.cn: 它们往往并不能那么轻易地对应起来。

lines.t: Moreover, understanding the brain is not the same as understanding the mind.
lines.cn: 此外，理解大脑并不等于理解心智。

lines.t: Some researchers have suggested that thoughts cannot properly be seen as purely internal.
lines.cn: 一些研究者提出，思想不能被恰当地视为纯粹内在的东西。

lines.t: Instead, thoughts make sense only in reference to the individual's external world.
lines.cn: 相反，思想只有参照个人的外部世界才有意义。

lines.t: So while there may be insights to be gained from matching behavior to brain activity, those insights will not necessarily lead to justice in a court of law.
lines.cn: 因此，尽管把行为与大脑活动对应起来或许能带来一些洞见，但这些洞见未必能带来法庭上的公正。

lines.t: Problems surround the use of machines to spot deception, at least until it has been rigorously tested.
lines.cn: 用机器识别欺骗存在诸多问题，至少在它经过严格检验之前是如此。

lines.t: A high-tech test that can tell when a person is not telling the truth sounds too good to be true.
lines.cn: 一种能判断出一个人是否说谎的高科技检测，听起来好得令人难以置信。

lines.t: And when something sounds too good to be true, it usually is.
lines.cn: 而事情一旦听起来好得难以置信，通常就确实不可信。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the island of Makalua?

options.A: Most of its residents speak several languages.
options.B: Some of its indigenous languages are dying out.
options.C: Each village there speaks a totally different language.
options.D: Its languages have interested researchers the world over.

questions.cn: 关于马库阿拉岛，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 其大多数居民会说好几种语言。
optionsCn.B: 它的一些土著语言正在消亡。
optionsCn.C: 那里每个村子讲的都是完全不同的语言。
optionsCn.D: 它的语言引起了全世界研究者的兴趣。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the talk about languages in the world?

options.A: They are spread randomly across the world.
options.B: Some are more difficult to learn than others.
options.C: More are found in tropical regions than in the mild zones.
options.D: They enrich and impact each other in more ways than one.

questions.cn: 关于世界上的语言，我们从讲话中了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们随机分布在世界各地。
optionsCn.B: 有些语言比其他语言更难学。
optionsCn.C: 热带地区的语言比温带地区多。
optionsCn.D: 它们以不止一种方式相互丰富和影响。

questions.stem: What have the diverse team of researchers found about the previous studies on language diversity?

options.A: They used different methods to collect and analyze data.
options.B: They identified distinct patterns of language distribution.
options.C: Their conclusions do not correspond to their original hypotheses.
options.D: There is no conclusive account for the cause of language diversity.

questions.cn: 这支多元的研究团队对以往关于语言多样性的研究发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们使用不同的方法收集和分析数据。
optionsCn.B: 它们识别出了语言分布的独特规律。
optionsCn.C: 它们的结论与最初的假设不符。
optionsCn.D: 对语言多样性的成因尚无定论。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Last week, I attended a research workshop on an island in the South Pacific.
lines.cn: 上周，我在南太平洋的一座岛上参加了一个研究研讨会。

lines.t: 30 people were present and all except me came from the island called Makalua in the nation of Vanuatu.
lines.cn: 在场有 30 人，除我之外都来自瓦努阿图共和国的马库阿拉岛。

lines.t: They live in 16 different communities and speak 16 distinct languages.
lines.cn: 他们生活在 16 个不同的社区，讲 16 种不同的语言。

lines.t: In many cases, you could stand at the edge of one village and see the outskirts of the next community yet the residents of each village speak a completely different language.
lines.cn: 很多时候，你站在一个村子的边上就能望见下一个社区的边缘，可每个村子的居民讲的却是完全不同的语言。

lines.t: According to recent work by my colleagues at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History, this island, just 100 kilometers long and 20 kilometers wide, is home to speakers of perhaps 40 different indigenous languages.
lines.cn: 根据我的同事们在马克斯·普朗克人类历史科学研究所最近的研究，这座仅长 100 公里、宽 20 公里的岛上，可能有 40 种不同土著语言的使用者。

lines.t: Why so many?
lines.cn: 为什么会这么多？

lines.t: We could ask this same question of the entire globe.
lines.cn: 我们可以把同样的问题放到整个地球上。

lines.t: People don't speak one universal language or even a handful.
lines.cn: 人们并没有讲一种通用的语言，甚至也不是只有几种。

lines.t: Instead, today our species collectively speaks over 7 ,000 distinct languages.
lines.cn: 相反，今天我们这个物种总共讲着 7000 多种不同的语言。

lines.t: And these languages are not spread randomly across the planet.
lines.cn: 而且这些语言并不是随机分布在地球上的。

lines.t: For example, far more languages are found in tropical regions than in the mild zones.
lines.cn: 例如，热带地区的语言数量远多于温带地区。

lines.t: The tropical island of New Guinea is home to over 900 languages.
lines.cn: 热带岛屿新几内亚拥有 900 多种语言。

lines.t: Russia, 20 times larger, has 105 indigenous languages.
lines.cn: 面积大 20 倍的俄罗斯有 105 种土著语言。

lines.t: Even within the tropics, language diversity varies widely.
lines.cn: 即使在热带地区内部，语言多样性也差异巨大。

lines.t: For example, the 250,000 people who live on Vanuatu's 80 islands speak 110 different languages.
lines.cn: 例如，生活在瓦努阿图 80 座岛上的 25 万人讲着 110 种不同的语言。

lines.t: But in Bangladesh, a population 600 times greater speaks only 41 languages.
lines.cn: 但在孟加拉国，人口是这个数字的 600 倍，却只讲 41 种语言。

lines.t: How come humans speak so many languages?
lines.cn: 人类为什么讲这么多语言？

lines.t: And why are they so unevenly spread across the planet?
lines.cn: 又为什么它们在地球上的分布如此不均？

lines.t: As it turns out, we have few clear answers to these fundamental questions about how humanity communicates.
lines.cn: 结果发现，对于人类如何交流这些根本问题，我们几乎没有明确的答案。

lines.t: Most people can easily brainstorm possible answers to these intriguing questions.
lines.cn: 大多数人很容易就能对这些引人入胜的问题想出一些可能的答案。

lines.t: They hypothesize that language diversity must be about history, cultural differences, mountains or oceans dividing populations.
lines.cn: 他们假设语言多样性必定与历史、文化差异、阻隔人群的山脉或海洋有关。

lines.t: But when our diverse team of researchers from six different disciplines and eight different countries began to review what was known, we were shocked that only a dozen previous studies had been done, including one we ourselves completed on language diversity in the Pacific.
lines.cn: 但当我们这支来自八个国家、六个不同学科的研究团队开始梳理已有知识时，我们惊讶地发现此前只做过十几项研究，其中包括我们自己完成的一项关于太平洋地区语言多样性的研究。

lines.t: These prior efforts all examined the degree to which different environmental, social and geographic variables correlated with the number of languages found in a given location.
lines.cn: 这些先前的研究都在考察不同的环境、社会和地理变量与某一地区语言数量之间的相关程度。

lines.t: The results varied a lot from one study to another, and no clear patterns emerged.
lines.cn: 各项研究结果差异很大，也没有出现清晰的规律。

lines.t: The studies also ran up against many methodological challenges, the biggest of which centered on the old statistical saying correlation does not equal causation.
lines.cn: 这些研究还遇到了许多方法上的难题，其中最大的难题围绕着一句古老的统计学格言：相关不等于因果。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do the surveys show about America according to the speaker?

options.A: Its middle-class is disappearing.
options.B: Its wealth is rationally distributed.
options.C: Its population is rapidly growing.
options.D: Its cherished dream is coming true.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，调查显示了美国的什么情况？

optionsCn.A: 它的中产阶级正在消失。
optionsCn.C: 它的人口正在快速增长。
optionsCn.D: 它所珍视的梦想正在实现。

questions.stem: What did Americans used to believe?

options.A: Success was but a dream without conscientious effort.
options.B: They could realize their dreams through hard work.
options.C: A few dollars could go a long way.
options.D: Wealth was shared by all citizens.

questions.cn: 美国人过去相信什么？

optionsCn.A: 没有认真的努力，成功只是梦想。
optionsCn.B: 他们可以通过努力工作实现梦想。
optionsCn.C: 几美元也能派上大用场。
optionsCn.D: 财富由所有公民共享。

questions.stem: What do low-income people aspire to?

options.A: Better working conditions.
options.B: Better-paying jobs.
options.C: High social status.
options.D: Full employment.

questions.cn: 低收入者期盼的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 更好的工作条件。
optionsCn.C: 很高的社会地位。
optionsCn.D: 全职就业。

questions.stem: What do businesses do to increase their revenues?

options.A: Reduce the administrative costs.
options.B: Adopt effective business models.
options.C: Hire part-time employees only.
options.D: Make use of the latest technology.

questions.cn: 企业为了增加收入会怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 降低管理成本。
optionsCn.C: 只雇用兼职员工。
optionsCn.D: 利用最新技术。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: We often hear people say that America is a land of opportunity, a country built on hope to aspire to greatness, on the American dream.
lines.cn: 我们常听人说，美国是一片充满机遇的土地，一个建立在憧憬卓越的希望之上、建立在美国梦之上的国家。

lines.t: But is the dream as we once knew it dying?
lines.cn: 但我们曾熟知的那个梦，是否正在消亡？

lines.t: Today's demographics show that the middle class is disappearing and now the richest 1% of the population has amassed more wealth than the bottom 90%.
lines.cn: 今天的人口统计数据显示，中产阶级正在消失，如今最富有的 1% 人口积累的财富已超过底层 90% 的总和。

lines.t: Once upon a time, Americans thought that if they worked hard enough, even in the face of adversity, they would be rewarded with success.
lines.cn: 曾几何时，美国人认为只要足够努力，即便身处逆境，也会得到成功的回报。

lines.t: These days though, the divide between rich and poor is greater than it has ever been.
lines.cn: 然而如今，贫富差距比以往任何时候都大。

lines.t: The question is, what is it going to take to change things?
lines.cn: 问题是，要改变现状需要付出什么？

lines.t: Maybe one day soon, real change will actually be made in our nation and the gap will be eradicated.
lines.cn: 也许不久的某一天，我们的国家会真正做出改变，差距将被消除。

lines.t: But what happens in the meantime?
lines.cn: 但在此期间又会怎样？

lines.t: Is there something that we can do to help close the gap?
lines.cn: 我们能不能做点什么来帮助缩小差距？

lines.t: Is there something that we can do to prove that a little compassion goes a long way?
lines.cn: 我们能不能做点什么来证明一点同情心也能大有作用？

lines.t: If we want to fix the problem of the income gap, first we have to understand it.
lines.cn: 如果我们想解决收入差距问题，首先必须理解它。

lines.t: It is a grim reality that you can have one person who only makes around $13 ,000 a year, while across town, another is making millions.
lines.cn: 一个严峻的现实是：有人一年只挣约 1.3 万美元，而城的另一头，有人却挣着数百万。

lines.t: For me, it is kind of astonishing.
lines.cn: 对我来说，这有点令人震惊。

lines.t: And if you ask low-income people what's the one thing that would change their life, they'll say a full-time job.
lines.cn: 如果你问低收入者，哪一件事能改变他们的生活，他们会说：一份全职工作。

lines.t: That's all they aspire to.
lines.cn: 这就是他们全部的期盼。

lines.t: So why is it so difficult for so many people to find employment?
lines.cn: 那么，为什么这么多人如此难以找到工作？

lines.t: It partly comes down to profit-driven business models that are built around low-wage work and part-time jobs that don't provide benefits.
lines.cn: 部分原因在于以利润驱动的商业模式，它们建立在低薪工作和不提供福利的兼职岗位之上。

lines.t: Businesses, in order to bolster profits, hire employees as part-time workers only.
lines.cn: 企业为了增加利润，只以兼职身份雇用员工。

lines.t: This means they are paid the lowest legal wage and receive no healthcare or other benefits provided to full-time employees.
lines.cn: 这意味着他们只能拿到最低法定工资，也得不到全职员工享有的医疗或其他福利。

lines.t: Simultaneously, technological advancement and a global economy has reduced the demand for well-paying blue-collar jobs here in the United States.
lines.cn: 与此同时，技术进步和全球化经济减少了美国本土对高薪蓝领岗位的需求。

lines.t: The cumulative effect of these two factors is that many Americans are forced to take two or more part-time jobs, just to make ends meet.
lines.cn: 这两个因素的累积效应是，许多美国人被迫做两份或更多兼职，仅仅为了维持生计。

lines.t: What has become obvious to me when it comes to the income gap is that there needs to be an opportunity for the people at the bottom to push them back up and push them into the middle class to give them hope in their lives.
lines.cn: 就收入差距而言，我越来越清楚的是：需要有一个机会，把底层的人重新拉起来、推入中产阶级，给他们的生活以希望。
